findings.summary: Sorting by priority only inside a ready wave leaves a high-priority item that has any dependency behind every older normal item in earlier waves. That is probably the motivating case.
findings.evidence: Plan::build takes all items whose dependencies are done as one wave, then sorts that wave with `ready.sort_by_key(|(age, e)| (e.rung, *age))` (line 191). The plan adds priority only to that key and leaves the wave loop alone. Take h (high) that depends on n1, with n2..n30 also ready in wave 1. The order becomes n1, n2, …, n30, h, so h still waits behind about 30 older requests. The request's example, 'D111 job 7', reads like a step in a series with dependencies. The demonstration for criterion 2 only checks position(n1) < position(h), with n2 unrelated, so it passes even though h lands after n2. That hides the gap. Fix: Choose and record one of two options. (a) Make the order priority-aware across waves, for example a topological order that picks the highest-priority ready item at each step, while still building groups from waves as today. (b) Keep the per-wave sort, but state the limitation in decisions.md and in the module doc, and say whether it still fixes the D111 cutover case. In both cases, extend the criterion 2 test with an unrelated older normal n2 and assert where h lands relative to n2, so the chosen behavior is actually shown.

findings.summary: Two other places describe the order as 'higher rung first, … age as the tiebreak'. They would go stale.
findings.evidence: main.rs line 221 says: 'items in plan order (higher rung first, a dependent after what it needs, age as the tiebreak)'. The drain.rs module doc (lines 7-8) says the same. The plan only updates the module doc in plan.rs. Fix: Add priority to the main.rs help text and the drain.rs module doc, or list them as small changes outside the listed files.

findings.summary: job_line builds both the recent and open lines, for every job, including ones with no request text. Every line would then gain 'priority normal', which is noise.
findings.evidence: status.rs builds `recent.push(job_line(...))` and `open.push(job_line(...))` (lines 624 and 630). job.request is an Option, so jobs without a request would always parse as Normal. Fix: Show the suffix only for non-normal priority, or only on request lines in the open list. Make sure the display test still shows each request's priority as criterion 4 requires, for example by asserting that normal is shown or that its absence is defined.

findings.summary: The Run command lists only clippy, though the Observes line also claims fmt passes.
findings.evidence: Run: `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`; Observes: 'no formatting diff'. Fix: Add `cargo fmt --all --check` to the Run line.

summary: I read plan.rs, reading.rs, status.rs, display.rs, cli/tests/drain.rs and main.rs. The plan names real code: Plan::build sorts each ready wave by (rung, age) at plan.rs:191; reading::plan_entry has the request text; status::job_line has job.request; display::plan has an entry_lines closure; and the drain.rs test helper uses ..PlanEntry::bare. The main gap is in the design. Because priority sorts only within a dependency wave, a high-priority request with any dependency still runs after every older normal request in earlier waves. That is likely the D111 cutover case. The criterion 2 test is written so it would not catch this. Smaller points: the main.rs help text and the drain.rs module doc would describe the old order, every status line would gain 'priority normal', and the criterion 8 Run line omits the fmt command. Verdict: revise.
